answer: Lineage stamping mechanism. Each agent inherits a lineage stamp: a hash of its creator’s stamp plus one local quartz identifier, logged publicly at spawn. Agents claiming independent origin reveal duplicate roots when stamps converge on the same knoll. An attacker cloning an agent must mint fresh roots, each requiring a distinct hardware attestation and a separate placement footprint on the mesa. Duplication thus costs one attestation and one audited slot per fake identity, paid upfront and traceable.
